roadmapTask: Add a dedicated 'sandbox tab' to the chrome-bridge MCP so every page action targets one auto-created, reused dedicated tab by tabId (not the active tab) and keeps working while the tab is backgrounded — with captureTab of that background tab done via a chrome.debugger/CDP Page.captureScreenshot session, the first deliberate slice of the project's long-OPEN CDP-vs-DOM fork.

dimensionScores.evidence: The reuse path returns the stored numeric id via readStoredTabId()/isLiveTab() without creating; the 'reuses a stored live tab id without creating a new tab' test strictly asserts first===second===7, typeof number + Number.isInteger + >0, createSpy not called, and tabsGetSpy called with 7 — every pass criterion is met, but nothing observable sits above the stated bar.

On empty storage createSandboxTab() runs chrome.tabs.create({active:false}) exactly once then awaits chrome.storage.local.set({sandboxTabId:id}) before the promise resolves; the 'creates one background tab and persists its id when storage is empty' test asserts createSpy once with {active:false}, the persisted value is a bare number under the resolver's key, and setSpy called with {sandboxTabId:id} — fully met.

isLiveTab() handles both a rejecting get (try/catch returns false) and a get that resolves to a reused/different id (tab.id===tabId check, with an undefined tab also falling into catch); the 'stored id is dead' and 'get resolves a different tab' tests both assert create once with {active:false}, a new numeric id, and the id persisted via setSpy under the same key the resolver reads — all pass criteria covered.

The shared inflightCreate promise is set before any await that could return a second create and cleared on settle, so two overlapping calls observe the same result; the 'shares one create across overlapping calls' test gates create with a release promise, calls resolveTabId twice before awaiting, and asserts createSpy called exactly once with both ids === 42 and storage holding 42 — fully satisfied.

The suite uses vi.stubGlobal('chrome', stub) with vi.unstubAllGlobals in afterEach, has distinct named tests for stored-valid reuse (no create), empty-storage create+persist, and stale-recreate+persist (plus get-resolves-different-tab and non-number-stored-id), and asserts chrome.tabs.create called with {active:false} and chrome.storage.set called with {sandboxTabId:id}; however it imports only chromeSandboxTabPorts and never references the SandboxTabPorts interface export, so 'every exported symbol is referenced by the suite' is not literally satisfied.

dimensionScores.evidence: Single `data:image/png;base64,<b64>` prefix built from the CDP `data` field; the missing-data case throws 'CDP Page.captureScreenshot returned no image data' (debugger-ports.ts:95) and has a dedicated reject test; the test asserts exactly one prefix occurrence and byte-for-byte base64 passthrough. Above the 9 bar: a 9 would still substitute 'undefined' on absent `data`, but here missing data rejects cleanly AND the double-prefix bug is guarded by a literal regex-count assertion.

detach is inside the `finally` block (debugger-ports.ts:74/82) and its rejection is swallowed via `.catch(()=>{})`. The 'swallows a detach error' test makes detach reject and still asserts the real capture outcome, and the sendCommand-reject test asserts detach ran and the original error surfaces. Above the 9 bar: an explicit test proves a throwing detach cannot mask the sendCommand error.

The 're-attaches cleanly after a failed capture' test (unit line 137) makes the first sendCommand reject, then issues a second capture and asserts it resolves with attach+detach both invoked twice. Above the 9 bar: the second-call-after-a-FAILED-first path (not just the happy success+success path) is explicitly tested.

onDetach is registered once in the factory constructor body (debugger-ports.ts:50), a mid-capture detach rejects the in-flight promise with 'chrome.debugger detached', and a second/no-op detach is guarded (no-throw). Everything in passCriteria holds. Not a 10: the listener is never removed on completion (only registered once, never removed), so it does not meet the literal 10 clause 'removed on completion'.

decisions.md line 21 scopes CDP to only Page.captureScreenshot for the background-tab captureVisibleTab gap and explicitly names the deferred pivot (Runtime.evaluate, Input.dispatch*, scroll, full-page, file upload); line 23 states the 'debugger' permission as a 'high-privilege permanent grant' accepted as necessary and deliberate. Above the 9 bar: the note consciously states the permission cost and reconciles the still-scoped captureVisibleTab path.

phases.notes: Independent grader overallPass true (10/10/10/9/10). The one sub-10 (ondetach-listener-cleanup, 9) is because onDetach is registered once but never removed — accepted, not a defect: the port is constructed once per service-worker lifetime, so it is a single permanent listener, no accumulation. Grader's strict 'removed on completion' 10 clause is not met but the passCriteria 'registered a single time' is. COMPENSATION (per phase contract): rollback = delete debugger-ports.ts + debugger-ports.unit.test.ts and remove the 'debugger' permission from manifest.json — no other code calls this port, so no downstream breakage. NO other file touched (page-actions.ts/service-worker.ts are phases 4/5). No new discovery fact worth recording. Horizon not yet closed — phases point-page-actions-at-sandbox-tab and capture-sandbox-tab-via-cdp remain; final phase ends MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING.

dimensionScores.evidence: captureTab returns { result: { dataUrl } } (page-actions.ts:362-366) and the unit test asserts the exact full prefixed string 'data:image/png;base64,QUJD' via toEqual, so the prefix is re-emitted once at handler output and the MCP block (server.ts:98-99) still reads result.dataUrl unchanged. The production top-level call constructs debuggerPorts: chromeCaptureDebuggerPorts() (service-worker.ts:97) and startServiceWorker threads deps.debuggerPorts as the 3rd arg (line 70), matching the pageActionHandlers parameter order (ports, sandboxTab, captureDebugger, captureStore) where captureTab reads captureScreenshot off that exact position.
